Why Data contracts are the new SLA: because the differentiated advantage has moved to the data layer and the operating model around it. The technology is the commodity; the discipline is the moat.

items: Expectations testing catches silent nulls before they become model incidents.
Column-level lineage answers regulator questions in hours.
Consolidation of duplicate pipelines is the fastest cost win in most estates.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: The expensive mistake is measurement retrofits: without the baseline locked in week one, every outcome claim becomes an argument instead of an audit, and the program loses its budget defense.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: Estates we modernize typically consolidate 30-50% of pipelines and halve batch windows.
Where this shows up in our work

This perspective is grounded in Lakehouse Architecture & Migration and Lakehouse Architecture & Migration within the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower — each carried by our platforms with governance and evidence built in.
